chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, who said:
I heard him saying: 'Whoever leaves the Two Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina) after the sun has risen, before he prays Dhuhr and Asr, a call will be made from behind him: May God not accompany you.'

key_terms.الْحَرَمَيْنِ: The Two Sanctuaries (referring to Mecca and Medina)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on leaving Mecca or Medina before praying Dhuhr and Asr?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the juristic preference (or strictness) regarding delaying departure from the Haramain until after Dhuhr and Asr prayers are completed, linking the physical act of leaving with a spiritual consequence. The 'call from behind' serves as a metaphorical warning of divine disapproval or the loss of spiritual companionship for those who rush out before fulfilling these specific prayer obligations. This ruling underscores the importance of integrating ritual prayer with the practical logistics of Hajj and Umrah in Shia fiqh.
